business_problem: Fresenius Digital Technology needed a scalable global IT support channel that improved user access and ticket resolution without adding a separate external technology stack.
solution_summary: Fresenius Digital Technology worked with Capgemini, ServiceNow, and Microsoft to build FreDi, a virtual-agent service layer for global IT support without adding a separate external stack. The program began with discovery workshops and requirement definition, then moved into a ServiceNow development cycle where the team iteratively built and tested the assistant against user feedback. FreDi was deployed inside the ServiceNow User Portal and Microsoft Teams so employees could open incidents, check ticket status, approve requests, or escalate to live agents from the same chat experience. The implementation emphasized transparent access across device types, future-ready architecture, and a seamless journey from request initiation to resolution. After launch, Capgemini provided hypercare while the virtual agent began handling large volumes of routine IT service interactions and surfacing chat popups when support teams updated tickets.

data_flow: Employees start IT support conversations in Microsoft Teams or the ServiceNow User Portal, where Virtual Agent and ServiceNow workflows create or update tickets, surface status information, route cases to live agents when needed, and push responses back through chat.
integration_points: Global IT Service Desk live agents
business_outcome: Fresenius Digital Technology created a high-volume virtual support channel that speeds IT interactions, increases chat-based ticket intake, and improves user experience without adding a new external stack.
